reviews.title: Want to transfer to a new device? Too bad.
reviews.text: It never occurred to the dev team that people get new phones. On competently designed authentication apps, there’s an easy method: on the old device, you tap export. On the new device, you tap import. One of the devices generates a QR code that you point  the other device at, then boom. Everything's transferred. This concept never occurred to this s dev team, apparently never encountered competently-designed authentication apps. Instead, you have to go to a desktop platform, which the instructions hopefully omit.

reviews.title: Why do you not support proven and safe Authenticators like everybody else?
reviews.text: ID.ME until recently supported third party authentication apps, like Authy that use standardized and proven protocols for authentication. Why do you have to come with your own proprietary app so that nobody can use their preferred authentication apps and is forced to install another authentication app. It doesn’t even support an encrypted backup or at least a mechanism to store the shared secrets. If you lose your phone, you’re back to the horrible verification process that could take weeks to process by ID.ME. It’s a shame that ID.ME is given this monopoly on “serving” the US government and they’re completely abusing this position for their own selfish gain.
